reason: Perianth scales (Cyperaceae, Amaranthaceae) are reduced perianth parts. They are not always undifferentiated tepals. Perianth (PO_0009058) is the safer bearer.
Gametophore branch is a bryophyte term. 'Branch stem' in flora texts means an ordinary branch of a vascular plant.
Same as R2952. The plural of 'branch stem' means ordinary branches, not gametophore branches.
A rudimentary ovary in a functionally staminate flower is a pistillode (a sterile pistil).
French 'rudiment d'ovaire' is the same concept as R2954.
'Rudimentary ovary' is the same concept as R2954.
A receptacular tube is a floral cup or tube bearing the perianth and stamens, which is a hypanthium.
The stigmatic surface is the receptive part of the stigma. Qualities such as papillose describe the stigma.
French 'plage stigmatique' means the stigmatic area, which is the stigma.
Plural of R2959.
A stigmatic zone is the receptive stigma region.
French 'zone stigmatique' means the stigmatic zone, as in R2961.
Interlacunar bundles are vascular bundles lying between air lacunae (Cyperaceae, Typha, aquatic plants).
Plural of R2963.
A pseudo-aril is an arilloid, a fleshy outgrowth of the seed that is not a true aril.
Same as R2965, without the hyphen.
The valves are parts of the spathe (Musa, Araceae, Commelina). Mapping them to the spathe puts valve qualities on the whole spathe. A valve-of-spathe part is needed, or the rule should be dropped.
Same as R2967. 'Valve of spathe' is a part of the spathe, not the spathe itself.
A culm sheath is a modified leaf sheath (bamboos, grasses), so its auricle is a leaf sheath auricle.
Hyphenated variant of R2969.
Word-order variant of R2969.

The epimatium is the fleshy aril-like outgrowth of the ovuliferous scale that covers the seed in Podocarpaceae. It is not the megasporophyll, which is the scale itself. No good existing PO term was found.
Plural of R2972. Epimatia are fleshy seed coverings, not megasporophylls.

reason: 'Palmate' says how the veins are arranged (venation pattern). The rule drops this and keeps only 'vein'.

reason: Same as R2974: the palmate arrangement is lost.

target: leaf lamina vein + palmate venation quality
reason: Same as R2974: the palmate arrangement is lost. 'Nerves' means veins.
PO_0006018 is the adaxial epidermis of a leaf. Other organs (petal, phyllode, stem) also have adaxial epidermis.
The target is leaf-only. Adaxial epidermis on other parts would be mislabelled.
'Upper epidermal layer' is a synonym of the leaf adaxial epidermis only when the part is a leaf.
A pod valve is a valve of a dehiscent fruit, which is a fruit valve.
Same as R2980.
French 'valve de la gousse' means pod valve.
Staminal scales are usually scale-like appendages or nectaries at the stamen base (Santalaceae, Ranunculaceae, Rhamnaceae), not the stamen itself. The microsporophyll reading holds only in conifers.
French 'écaille staminale' is ambiguous. It is a microsporophyll only for conifer cones, so it is doubtful for a general rule.
An accessory bundle is an additional vascular bundle.
Same as R2985.
A racemose branch of a panicle or compound inflorescence is a higher-order inflorescence axis. 'Inflorescence branch' is a synonym.
A racemiform branch is a branch of the inflorescence, as in R2987.
A leaf fascicle is a short shoot bearing a leaf cluster (Pinus, Larix, Berberis).
An axillary leaf fascicle is a short shoot in a leaf axil.
A leaf cluster can be a rosette or a terminal tuft, not necessarily on a short shoot. Only 'fascicle' reliably means a short shoot.
The gynostegial corona (Apocynaceae) is a corona derived from the stamens, so it is a staminal corona.
Latin/French 'corona staminea' means staminal corona.
'Perigyn' is a Carex term for the perigynium (the sac around the pistillate flower).
French 'périgyne' is mostly an adjective meaning perigynous (flower type). It is the perigynium only as a noun for sedges.
The target is a shoot-borne root spine, a palm term (Acanthorhiza). 'Root thorn' can mean any spine-like root, so the target is too specific.
Same as R2996. The target is specific to shoot-borne roots (palms).
Plural of R2996, with the same problem.
Laminal papillae are papillae of the leaf epidermis, which are leaf papilla cells (bryophytes).
'Lamina papillae' means papillae on the leaf lamina, as in R2999.
